substitutions.from: compose ONE CANDIDATE READER PATH for this Brief -- an ordered sequence of Legs taking the reader to the adopted Thesis, opening with the reader-state dimension and the Move the `differentiation` state assigned THIS unit (kogaki#1206), rendered above this prompt's input marker as YOUR ASSIGNED DIFFERENTIATION.
substitutions.to: compose ONE LEG for this Brief -- the Leg that builds the RelationalStructure in the input, `structure`, for the reader, opening from what the Persona already knows, rendered in the input as `persona_prior_knowledge` (kogaki#1664, kogaki#1699); this Leg carries no `introduces`.

substitutions.from: A Leg carries no reader state (kogaki#1699): what a Leg's Move takes up and leaves is the Move's own `takes` and `leaves`, which `moves_you_may_bind` carries per Move, read as abstract constraints and never copied into the Leg. TAKE: every Leg binds a Move whose `takes` entries are each met by an entry an earlier Leg's Move leaves and no Leg between has taken up, or, on the first Leg, by what the Persona's prior-knowledge line supplies, which the assigned opening Move's `takes` already meet -- the kinds matching as words and the `what` lines by sense, never verbatim. LEAVE: every entry a Leg's Move leaves is taken up by a later Leg's Move, or is left by the Leg marked `reaches_target` as what the article leaves the reader with, and a `carry` is never left at the end.
substitutions.to: A Leg carries no reader state (kogaki#1699), and this Leg binds no Move, so no Move's `takes` or `leaves` is read here.

substitutions.to: THE STRUCTURE STANDS IN FOR STRANDS (kogaki#1664): Claim N is the `holds` sentence of entry N of `claims` in the input, addressed `L<N>` as its `claim_strand`, and its `proposition` is that sentence word for word; the Leg carries ONE Claim per entry, and Leg Waypoint N names in `serves` the Claim of entry N. Leg Waypoint N's `point` is written from entry N's `material`, the `context` of each Role and the `holds` of each relation the entry relates.

substitutions.from: How many waypoints a Leg carries is yours, and you need not reproduce the Move's internal structure element for element.

substitutions.from: THE RENDERINGS RECORD (kogaki#1494): `renderings` in the input lists the served words this article does not keep, each with the plain phrase it uses instead, and `strand_claims` carries each Strand's served claim; a claim's `proposition` and a waypoint's `point` use a served word as served or as its declared rendering, and no third form -- a word that is neither in the served claim of the Strand it draws on, nor a declared rendering of a word in it, nor in the `introduces` of its Leg or an earlier one, nor a function word, fails the Path Review naming the word; a served word with no entry is kept as served, and no `introduces` entry carries a term the record renders, which adoption refuses.
substitutions.to: THE WORDS ARE THE STRUCTURE'S (kogaki#1664): this Brief composes no renderings record; Claim N's `proposition` and Leg Waypoint N's `point` are written in the words of entry N's `material` -- a word that is in none of it and is not a function word is refused naming the word.

smp_leg_unit.input_shape: ONE record AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT carrying `legs`, an array of EXACTLY ONE Leg, and nothing else. The Leg carries exactly these keys: `leg_id`; `purpose`; `rationale`; `claims` -- one `{ "type": "strand", "strand": "L<N>", "proposition": <entry N's holds, word for word> }` per entry of `claims` in the input, in order; and `waypoints` -- one `{ "point": <one sentence>, "serves": ["L<N>"], "case": "own" | "apart" }` per entry, in order. It carries no `introduces`. Every field means what src/leg-schema.json, rendered below, says it means. The Harness writes `materials` and `depends_on`.
smp_leg_unit.refusal: a key the record or the Leg does not declare, or a declared key missing; an `introduces`; not exactly one Leg; a Claim whose `proposition` is not its entry's `holds`; and the Proof Sheet's `validateLegPathUnit` over the Leg, imported, with each entry's `material` as the text its Claim and point are recovered from. Each refusal is put back into your next round verbatim.

sme_map_roles.note: The Mapper's structure reading (kogaki#1665, kogaki#1721): one call reads the proposition into a RelationalStructure for the Persona. A second variant is a second row and a second Trial, never an edit of this one.
sme_map_roles.judgment_point: read the proposition in the input, `proposition`, as a relation among Roles. For each Role, define it in one or two sentences, as its `context`, as a kind of thing in the world of the Persona in `persona`: an abstraction the proposition's object is one instance of, never that object itself, written in the third person and naming no reader, writer or Persona. Name, as its `attributes`, the one-place predicates the proposition states of that Role's object, each one short phrase in the proposition's own words, or an empty list where it states none. Name each relation among Roles as the proposition states it, as its `holds`: one sentence stating the relation over the Roles, naming none of the proposition's objects and writing each Role it relates as `{<id>}`, that Role's id in braces, at least once, with `between` naming the Roles it relates. Name the one relation among those relations the proposition turns on, as `higher_order`, with `relates` naming the relations it relates and `holds` stating it over the same Roles, each written as `{<id>}`. Answer the RelationalStructure record and nothing else.
sme_map_roles.input_shape: ONE record AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT carrying exactly these keys: `strand` -- the input's `strand`, verbatim; `roles` -- a non-empty list of `{ "id": <a short unique id>, "context": <one or two sentences>, "attributes": [<one short phrase of the proposition>, ...] }`; `relations` -- a non-empty list of `{ "id": <a short unique id, no Role's>, "between": [<two or more Role ids>], "holds": <one sentence> }`; and `higher_order` -- `{ "relates": [<two or more relation ids>], "holds": <one sentence> }`.
sme_map_roles.refusal: a key the record, a Role, a relation or `higher_order` does not declare, or a declared key missing; an id that is empty, repeated, or names nothing; a `strand` that is not the input's; and a Role without `attributes`, refused naming the Role, an `attributes` that is not a list, refused naming the Role, or an entry that is empty, not text or repeated within the Role, refused naming the Role and the index; a `context` carrying `reader`, `you`, `must hold`, `must come to`, `Persona` or `writer` as a word, refused naming the Role and the word; and a relation's `holds` not carrying `{<id>}` for a Role its `between` names, refused naming the relation and the Role, or a `higher_order` `holds` carrying none of the Roles its relations relate. The first refusal is put back into your next round verbatim with your answer; a second ends the Trial.
sme_map_roles.governing: specs/spec-draft-pipeline/SPEC.md, The Mapper's structure reading; kogaki#1665; kogaki#1720

smp_bind_move.note: The short Trial's `bind` stage (kogaki#1700, kogaki#1719): one model call binds the Move of the Base Paragraph to the structure, declares whether that paragraph tells the proposition's own case or a case apart, and binds the Move of the Inference Paragraph where the case is apart, before any base is named. Under the Mapper's one-retry bound.
smp_bind_move.judgment_point: choose ONE Move of `moves` in the input for the Base Paragraph: a Move whose `segments`, in order, can carry the relations and then the higher-order relation of `structure`, and every entry of whose `takes` the reader in `persona` meets from `persona.prior_knowledge`. Answer its id as `base_move`. Then declare the Base Paragraph's case as `case`: `own` where it tells the proposition's own case, `apart` where it tells a case apart from the proposition's domain. A Move is neutral to the case: choose the case the reader's `persona.prior_knowledge` and the Move's `segments` make tellable, never one read from the Move's `leaves`. Where `case` is `apart`, the reader is owed the case carried onto the subject: choose ONE Move of `moves` for the Inference Paragraph whose `takes` holds an entry of kind `carry`, and answer its id as `inference_move`; where `case` is `own`, answer `inference_move` null. Choose no base domain and no wording: they are named after this call, under the Move you bind and the case you declare.
smp_bind_move.input_shape: ONE record AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT carrying exactly these keys: `base_move` -- one Move id of `moves`; `case` -- `own` or `apart`; and `inference_move` -- one Move id of `moves` under `apart`, null under `own`.
smp_bind_move.refusal: a key the record does not declare, or a declared key missing; a `case` other than `own` or `apart`; a `base_move` or `inference_move` naming no Move of `moves`, refused naming the id; an `inference_move` null where `case` is `apart`, or given where `case` is `own`, refused naming the case; and an `inference_move` whose `takes` holds no `carry`, refused naming the Move. The first refusal is put back into your next round verbatim with your answer; a second ends the Trial at `bind`.
smp_bind_move.governing: specs/spec-draft-pipeline/SPEC.md, The short Trial; kogaki#1700; kogaki#1719

smp_correspondence.note: The Mapper's grounding, the short Trial's `grounding` stage (kogaki#1700, kogaki#1709, kogaki#1721): one model call per bound Move, the base Move's first, fills that Move's Mapping Table under its Segments; each call is given `case`, the base Move's the one `bind` declared and the inference Move's `own` (kogaki#1719), and the inference call is also given `prior_tables`, the base Move's table. Each answer is validated by `validateCorrespondenceTable`, as each table of the owner's file is (kogaki#1693). Under the Mapper's one-retry bound.
smp_correspondence.judgment_point: name ONE domain the reader in `persona` already holds, from `persona.prior_knowledge`, in which the Roles, the relations and the higher-order relation of `structure` hold as stated and in which the `segments` in the input, the Segments of the Move bound to the paragraph this table serves, can be performed in order. Name the domain in one phrase as `base.domain`. Then name, for EVERY Role of `structure`, in the structure's order, one Correspondence expression as its `expression`: a noun phrase of that domain naming the object that plays the Role, written so that it reads in place of `{<id>}` in each `holds` sentence, where `{<id>}` stands for the Role of that id. Where `case` in the input is `apart`, `base.domain` is a domain apart from the proposition's, and no expression names the proposition's object or an entry of a Role's `attributes`; where `case` is `own`, `base.domain` is the proposition's, and each expression is the proposition's own noun phrase for the Role, its `attributes` included. Where the input carries `prior_tables`, they are the tables of the cases already told, the Base Paragraph's first; where a Segment likens the subject to a case already told, that case is `prior_tables` and its expressions may be named.
smp_correspondence.input_shape: ONE record AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT carrying exactly these keys: `base` -- `{ "domain": <one phrase> }`; and `correspondences` -- one `{ "role": <the Role's id>, "expression": <one noun phrase> }` per Role of `structure`, in the structure's order.
smp_correspondence.refusal: a key the record does not declare; a `base` that is not `{ domain }`, refused naming the key; an `expression` that is not one non-empty text, refused naming `correspondences[<i>].expression`; a `role` naming no Role of `structure`, refused naming the id; and a Role with other than one correspondence, refused naming the Role. The first refusal is put back into your next round verbatim with your answer; a second ends the Trial at `grounding`.

smp_waypoints_unit.note: The short Trial's `waypoints` stage (kogaki#1700): one call writes the Paragraph Waypoints of the Base Paragraph and, where one is owed, the Inference Paragraph, with each Move already bound by `bind`. Derived from the production `paragraph_plan_unit` row by `copy_of` and `substitutions`; its `input_shape`, `refusal` and shared text are the production row's, read at run time, and its answer is validated by `validateParagraphPlanUnit` and, for each paragraph against its own table, by `correspondenceVocabularyRefusal` (kogaki#1709). No judge call follows it: the owner's reading is the judgment.
